newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB's Feb debentures seen at 2.35 pct - bankers.
newsitem.headline: NCB's Feb debentures seen at 2.35 pct - bankers.

text.p: The coupon rate for Nippon Credit Bank Ltd"s February five-year bank debentures is likely to be set at 2.35 percent, up from 2.15 percent for its January issues, officials from long-term credit banks said on Thursday.
This compares with a coupon rate of 1.6 percent for the Industrial Bank of Japan's February five-year debentures.
The Nippon Credit Bank (NCB) is likely to leave its long-term prime rate for February unchanged at a record low of 2.5 percent, the officials said.

Attention had been focused on whether or not NCB would raise the coupon rate for its new five-year debentures, as the deviation of the market yield of its January debentures from its coupon rate had widened recently.
NCB"s January five-year debentures were offered at 4.0 percent on Wednesday.
The spread between the coupon rate of NCB debentures and the Industrial Bank of Japan"s (IBJ) debentures will widen to 0.75 percent, up from 0.55 percent previously.
The IBJ debenture is the benchmark in the market.
The Nippon Credit Bank will officially announce its February long-term prime rate and terms for its new five-year bank debentures at 2 p.m. (0500 GMT).
